newsitem.title: UK: Taxotere said more effective in breast cancer.
newsitem.headline: Taxotere said more effective in breast cancer.

text.p: Rhone Poulenc Rorer Inc's cancer drug Taxotere is more effective in treating metastatic breast cancer than the current standard treatment, Pharmacia & Upjohn Inc's Adriamycin, British scientists said on Wednesday.

Stephen Chan, a clinical oncologist at the City Hospital Breast Clinic in Nottingham, England, said in a statement that Phase III trial data indicated that Taxotere was "the first drug shown in a clinical study to be more effective" than Adriamycin.

In a presentation to the American Society of Clinical Oncology ASCO) in Denver, Colorado, Chan said patients who received Taxotere showed a 50 percent better overall response rate compared with patients given Adriamycin.
Metastatic breast cancer is the leading cause of death for women between the ages of 40 and 55 in the U.S, with 45,000 deaths a year.

Chan said 326 patients were involved in the study at a number of sites. He said that of 161 patients receiving Taxotere 63 had a partial response, meaning a reduction of at least 50 percent in measurable tumour size.
Another 13 showed a complete response, which means the complete disappearance of all clinical and radiological signs of tumour, although not a cure.
Of 165 women given Adriamycin, 45 showed a partial response and seven a complete response.
Chan told the conference that Taxotere showed a lower incidence of nausea, vomiting and stomatitis, while Adriamycin showed a lower incidence of diarrhoea.
